### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, exactly one of the three alternatives A14, A15 and A20 ran in each case (about 38, 32 and 30 in 100 cases respectively — the shares sum to one per case), placed about 60% of the way through the case's events. In the later window the one-of-three pattern is unchanged (about 34, 35 and 32 in 100 cases), but the alternative now sits about 32% of the way through. [POS001, POS002, POS003]
- The order between this alternative block and A21/A22 flipped completely: before, in every case containing both (about 31–38 in 100), A21 or A22 always came first and the reverse never occurred; in the later window the alternative always comes first (about 32–35 in 100) and the reverse never occurs. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- In the earlier window A21 immediately followed A40 (event distance 1 in every case); in the later window the distance is 2 in every case, consistent with the alternative step now sitting between them. [LAG004]
- The late segment tightened: before, the A22→A23 distance was 1 in about 48 in 100 cases and 2 otherwise, the A23→A27 distance was 2 in about 48 in 100, and A22→A27 was always 3; in the later window A23 immediately follows A22 and A27 immediately follows A23, so A22→A27 is always 2. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- A21, A22 and A23 still occur in every case, each shifting only slightly later in relative position (about +0.01 to +0.03). [POS004, POS005, POS006]
- A10 and A11 still appear in every case, but they repeat less in the later window: mean occurrences per case fell from about 1.9 to about 1.6, and the share of cases with repeats fell from about 47 to about 38 in 100. [OCC001, OCC002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Screening tested 47 control-flow units and 18 items qualified, against roughly 0.23 expected if nothing had changed, so the volume of findings is far beyond what random re-splits of a stable process produce. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the per-case choice step — exactly one of A14, A15 and A20 — is now executed much earlier in the case, between A40 and A21 (about a third into the case), whereas in the earlier window it ran after A21 and A22, around the A22–A23–A27 segment (about 60% into the case). Supporting signs: the order against A21 and A22 flipped from always A21/A22-first to always alternative-first across all six relation pairs [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]; the alternatives' mean relative position dropped from about 0.60 to about 0.32 [POS001, POS002, POS003]; the A40→A21 distance grew from 1 to 2 while the A22→A23→A27 distances collapsed to a fixed 1 [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]; and each alternative's participation (about one case in three, one alternative per case) is stable across windows, which fits a relocation rather than an activity being added, removed or taken more often [POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL003, REL005]. Limitations: positions and lags are event ranks, not clock times, so this is a reordering within the case and says nothing about timing; and without direct-successor evidence the data cannot show exactly which activity each alternative now follows beyond the observed pairs, so a broader re-sequencing of the A40–A27 segment moving additional unobserved steps cannot be ruled out.

Other differences: A10 and A11 occur in every case in both windows but repeat less often in the later window (mean occurrences per case about 1.9 down to about 1.6; cases with repeats down from about 47 to about 38 in 100). No relational item links this repetition change to the relocation above, so it is reported separately. [OCC001, OCC002]
